newsitem.title: FRANCE: Two hurt in Le Pen incident near Paris.
newsitem.headline: Two hurt in Le Pen incident near Paris.

text.p: Two people, one a Socialist parliamentary candidate, were injured on Friday during a clash involving extreme-rightist leader Jean-Marie Le Pen in a troubled Paris suburb, officials said.
The candidate, Anette Peulvast-Bergeal, was slightly injured, the officials said. The identity of the other victim was not immediately known.
Radio reports quoted friends of the injured woman saying Le Pen himself had struck her but his aides denied this.

During the incident, anti-racist militants hurled eggs and stones at Le Pen, who was touring the area to support his daughter Marie Caroline Le Pen, candidate for the National Front (FN) in the outer suburb of Mantes-la-Jolie.

Eyewitnesses said several dozen members of the "Ras-le-Front" (Enough of the Front) group shouted insults at Le Pen when he arrived in the area two days before Sunday's decisive National Assembly runoffs.
Bodyguards and police surrounded the National Front leader to protect him from the missiles, none of which apparently struck him.
Le Pen, who had to take refuge in a cafe, seemed unhurt but was heard to shout angrily: "When I'm attacked, I've never been afraid of another man or even several at once."

Police in the southern town of Orange, one of four French municipalities with an FN mayor, said a fire was intentionally set at a National Front office overnight and two party members had been overcome by smoke.
The blaze followed a fistfight between pro and anti-Le Pen militants at a local outdoor market earlier in the day.
